If multiple demos show a rectangular frame with missing edge cells recolored, test the foreground bounding box's perimeter as the candidate rule: recolor only background cells on its min/max row or column, never the interior, and accept it only if it exactly reproduces every demo.

A plausible rule is not validated until these checks pass. Then revise the rule to account for mismatches, requesting a discriminating demo when evidence remains ambiguous. After every edit, rerun all demo regressions. If the demos do not establish the rule (including when the cap is exhausted), keep uncertainty explicit and don't call a heuristic verified. For ray/extension rules, check which object sends the continuation and where it stops; don't extend based only on foreground occupancy or add unverified companion fills.
4. Run the transform on the full test grid; assert dimensions, rectangularity, and cell range before submitting exactly the program-produced grid. Do not hand-transcribe a grid for submission: a transcription mistake can make a valid ARC answer malformed. If validation fails, fix the input/output serialization and rerun the program; if no transform reproduces every available demo, leave the task file unchanged. Save a validated replacement only when the instance ends as directed, and confirm the write.
5. On every turn, emit only one action JSON object as the entire reply, without commentary or markdown. Request demos when evidence is needed; submit only grids produced by the task program; use `finish` only after the instance is over. Never add explanatory prose around the action JSON.
